title: Independence of the sheaf K-flat resolution after exact point sections
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with final object $U$, let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and suppose $\Gamma=\Gamma(U,-)$ is exact on abelian sheaves. Let $R$ be a commutative ring with a map $R\to\Gamma(\mathcal O)$, choose $t\in R$, put $A=R/(t)$, and suppose
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal O\xrightarrow{t}\mathcal O\longrightarrow\mathcal O'\longrightarrow0$$
is exact, with $\mathcal O'=\mathcal O/t\mathcal O$. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], their derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived extension $T=-\otimes_{\mathcal O}^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O'$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Exact sections induce $G:D(\mathcal O)\to D(R)$ and $G':D(\mathcal O')\to D(A)$ by restriction along the displayed coefficient maps. Put $L=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}A$ [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor]. For a K-flat complex $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], put $C=\Gamma(P)$. The quotient identification $P\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'=P/tP$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and exact sections give $\theta_P:C/tC\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(P/tP)$. Define
$$\alpha_P=\theta_P\circ c_C:LG(P)\longrightarrow G'T(P),$$
where $c_C:L(Q_R C)\to Q_A(C/tC)$ is the universal derived-tensor counit of [lem-pc-mixed-tensor-pointwise-left-derived], specialized to the second factor $A[0]$ and followed by $C\otimes_R A\cong C/tC$, with $Q_R,Q_A$ the localization functors, and using the canonical identification $T(P)=P/tP$. Then for every chain map $h:P\to P'$ between such complexes,
$$G'T(h)\circ\alpha_P=\alpha_{P'}\circ LG(h).$$
For every complex $M$ and two K-flat resolutions $p:P\to M$, $p':P'\to M$ with flat terms, the maps
$$G'T(p)\circ\alpha_P\circ LG(p)^{-1},\qquad G'T(p')\circ\alpha_{P'}\circ LG(p')^{-1}$$
from $LG(M)$ to $G'T(M)$ are equal in $D(A)$. This equality is with respect to the canonical derived-extension identifications specified by $p,p'$; it asserts coherence of the displayed comparisons, without asserting they are isomorphisms.
